Guidance: Record the contractor, the contract number and type, the reporting period covered, and the report submission date. The contract type determines whether a cost forecast is expected.
Describe the progress on scope made during this reporting period.
Identify any quality or performance variances.

Describe whether the contract is on budget. If over or under budget, identify the cause of the variance.

List any risks. Risks should also be recorded in the project risk register.
Identify planned corrective or preventive actions necessary to recover schedule, cost, scope, or quality variances.
